title: "Lecture 7 Team Projects"
subtitle: "Interest-Rate Models"

## Project 1: Vasicek as a Risk Scenario Generator

**Scenario.** Explain what a mean-reverting short-rate model can and cannot say about future rates.

**Objectives.** Choose defensible parameters; interpret mean reversion and volatility; compare one-year model distributions with historical changes.

**Sources.** Monthly short rates from [Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/categories/22) or the [Bank of Canada](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/interest-rates/). If the series cannot be downloaded, use the documented monthly observations and Vasicek parameters in the [Lecture 7 fallback rate-model dataset](fallback_data/lecture-7-rate-models.csv).

**Deliverables.** Parameter rationale, distribution and three paths, historical comparison, model-risk memo, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Parameters 25; interpretation 25; scenarios 20; validation and model risk 20; presentation 10.

## Project 2: Why Hull–White Must Fit Today's Curve

**Scenario.** Evaluate a proposal to price a callable bond without first matching current market prices.

**Objectives.** Distinguish equilibrium and no-arbitrage models; demonstrate the importance of curve fit; interpret mean-reversion and volatility effects.

**Sources.** Current curve data from the [U.S. Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView), [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/categories/115), or the [Bank of Canada](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/interest-rates/canadian-bonds/). If a curve and calibration output are unavailable, use the documented curve nodes and Hull–White assumptions in the [Lecture 7 fallback rate-model dataset](fallback_data/lecture-7-rate-models.csv).

**Deliverables.** Model comparison, curve-fit exhibit, two sensitivities, instrument-specific recommendation, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Model distinction 25; curve-fit reasoning 25; sensitivities 20; recommendation 20; presentation 10.

## Project 3: Model Choice for an ALM Committee

**Scenario.** Choose between historical scenarios, Vasicek, and Hull–White for a pension plan's asset-liability analysis.

**Objectives.** Match each method to purpose; compare calibration, curve consistency, interpretability, and tail behavior; recommend a primary model and challenger.

**Sources.** A public pension plan's asset-liability disclosures and curves from [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/categories/115) or the [Bank of Canada](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/interest-rates/canadian-bonds/). If no complete case is available, use the pension facts and historical, Vasicek, and Hull–White outputs documented in the [Lecture 7 fallback rate-model dataset](fallback_data/lecture-7-rate-models.csv).

**Deliverables.** Requirements matrix, three-model comparison, scenario evidence, governance recommendation, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Problem framing 20; model comparison 30; evidence 20; governance and recommendation 20; presentation and sourcing 10.

## Project 4: Stress-Test Mean Reversion

**Scenario.** A risk manager doubts that a single estimated mean-reversion speed is stable enough for decisions.

**Objectives.** Estimate parameters over contrasting periods; interpret estimation uncertainty; test portfolio values under slow, base, and fast mean reversion.

**Sources.** Monthly short rates from [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/categories/22) or the [Bank of Canada](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/interest-rates/). If live data or portfolio cash flows are unavailable, use the documented observations, bond cash flows, and parameter cases in the [Lecture 7 fallback rate-model dataset](fallback_data/lecture-7-rate-models.csv).

**Deliverables.** Sample-period comparison, parameter table, three valuation scenarios, limitation note, risk-limit recommendation, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Data design 20; parameter reasoning 25; stress analysis 25; decision implications 20; presentation and reproducibility 10.
